title: Delayed Metronome Rating Causes Zero Amount Stripe Invoice
content: When Metronome rates usage late after Stripe invoice finalized, Stripe invoice amount is 0 but Metronome shows 1200 rated usage. Example invoice in_123 amount 0 because rated_at 02:40 is 95 mins after finalized_at 01:05. Delayed rating zero amount next invoice catchup.

title: Commit True-Up Rule - Commit Applies Next Invoice - Commit Remaining
content: If invoice charged 1200 when commit remaining 4000, check true-up rule commit_applies_next_invoice. Commit $10000 with $6000 consumed $4000 remaining does not reduce current invoice. Charged 1200 commit remaining true-up next invoice.

title: Currency Mismatch Between Metronome and Stripe EUR USD
content: Currency mismatch EUR USD causes invoice amount mismatch. Metronome currency EUR vs Stripe currency USD subsidiary currency mismatch EUR USD. Invoice in_789 currency mismatch.

title: Credits Apply Before Usage Overage
content: When an invoice is higher than the remaining commit credit, compare rated usage with the credit balance. Credits apply first and only usage above the available balance is charged. Example rated usage 800 less credit balance 500 produces invoice usage charge 300. Check credit balance, commit consumption, and overage rule.

title: Tax Added to Usage Invoice
content: A Stripe invoice can exceed Metronome rated usage when tax is configured as exclusive. Compare the usage line with the tax line and check tax behavior, tax rate, and tax amount. Example 800 rated usage plus 40 sales tax at 5 percent gives a total invoice of 840. Tax is separate from rated usage.

title: Duplicate Usage Event Increases Rated Amount
content: If an invoice usage amount is higher than expected, inspect event ingestion for duplicate usage events and retries. Compare rated usage with the source event IDs and duplicate event count. A repeated event may cause usage to be rated more than once; verify idempotency and request a rating correction if confirmed.
